extracted.intended_audience: policy analysts, DoD contracting officers, auditors, and legislators evaluating OMB Circular A-76 implementations
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating DoD decisions and outcomes when commercial functions are competitively sourced under OMB Circular A-76, focusing on cost-comparison decision rules, post-award cost changes, and effects on federal employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: A-76 decision rule: contract when more economical
rubrics_metrics.description: In accordance with OMB Circular A-76, DOD performs cost comparisons and contracts out commercial functions when the comparisons show that contracting is more economical than in-house performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires a cost comparison analysis comparing in-house performance costs to contract costs; the outcome (contract vs in-house) should be determined by whether contracting is more economical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-award contract cost increases and net savings
rubrics_metrics.description: All but one of the functions reviewed had subsequent contract cost increases but savings were still realized on 17 of the functions; savings were not realized on two functions and GAO could not determine whether savings were realized on one function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluations should track contract costs after award and compare projected savings to actual post-award costs to determine whether net savings were realized. Document cases with cost increases and assess whether initial savings estimates remain valid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee outcome metrics after conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: Of 2,535 employees affected in a random sample of 31 functions converted to contract, 1,881 (74%) obtained other government positions; most of the remaining employees resigned, retired, or obtained employment with contractors; only 129 (5%) were involuntarily separated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess and report the distribution of employee outcomes following conversion (reassignment to other government jobs, resignation, retirement, contractor employment, involuntary separation) and compute rates/percentages to evaluate the human impact of contracting decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation sampling and timeframe considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: GAO reviewed a judgmental sample of 20 functions contracted out between Oct. 1, 1978 and Feb. 28, 1981, and a random sample of 31 functions converted during fiscal year 1983.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing A-76 implementations, specify sampling methods (judgmental vs random), sample sizes, and time periods covered; these design choices affect the generalizability and interpretation of findings about cost outcomes and employee effects.
